bankDebitsCurrency: Bank payments are available for USD and CAD.
bankDebitsHelp: US bank accounts (ACH) for USD, Canadian bank accounts (pre-authorized debit) for CAD. This switch turns bank payments on and off. Your Stripe account must have the method activated; turning it off in the Stripe Dashboard doesn't remove it here.
bankDebitsWarning: Stripe refused bank payments on {date}, so members were offered cards only. Turn on ACH Direct Debit or Pre-authorized debits in your Stripe Dashboard.
sms.capHelp: From 1 to 100,000 send attempts per day in the gym's timezone (default 1,000). Failed or uncertain attempts also count. Further member texts are refused and counted in System health. Owner test texts are exempt.
sms.capSaved: The daily text cap is saved.
title: Integrations
intro: Only owners can change these. Saved passwords and keys are never shown again.
error: The request failed. Please try again.
conflict: Settings changed elsewhere. The latest saved settings are shown; review them and try again.
conflictKept: Something changed elsewhere, so this change wasn’t saved. Your entries are still here; reload to see the latest settings, then try again.
timeout: The request took too long to answer and may still have gone through. Reload and check the settings before trying again.
sandbox: This sandbox uses the demo’s email, SMS and payment services. Integration credentials can’t be changed here. You can change the daily text cap.
operatorManaged: Whoever runs this install manages email, SMS and payments, so their credentials can’t be changed here. Ask them if any need to change. You can change the daily text cap.
sms.title: SMS
sms.stored: Credentials are stored securely and are never shown again. Enter them again to replace the settings.
sms.unreadable: Your stored SMS settings could not be read. Replace or remove them.
sms.hint: Use your gym’s own upgraded Twilio account and an SMS-capable number it owns. Register your sender with the provider before sending. Each text, including this test, costs your gym.
sms.testHint: Enter the number you want to test, including its country code (for example +1). Only that number receives this test. Settings are saved after the account check and test both succeed.
sms.testHintNoCountry: Your gym has no country code set in Settings → Gym details, so a test number without + uses the From number's country code.
sms.saved: Test text accepted. SMS settings are saved.
sms.testFailed: The account check or test text failed. Check your credentials and registered sender; nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_authentication: Twilio denied access. Check the Account SID and copy the live auth token or API key credentials from the Twilio Console. If you use an API key, check that it can list and send messages. A new or upgraded Twilio account is also refused until its Primary Customer Profile is approved in Twilio’s Trust Hub. Nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_authentication_custom: The provider denied access. Check the Account SID and use live credentials issued by the provider at the configured URL. If you use an API key, check that it can list and send messages. Nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_trial_account: A Twilio trial account can send only Twilio templates to verified numbers. Upgrade a trial account to send this test text. If your account is already upgraded, verify the test number or get its Primary Customer Profile approved in Twilio’s Trust Hub. The account also needs its own SMS-capable number as the sender. Nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_sender: The test text failed: the From number isn't an SMS-capable number on this account, or the Messaging Service SID is wrong. Nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_recipient: The test text failed: the provider refused the test number. Check the number and its country code, and that the account may text that country. Nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_opted_out: The test text failed: the test number replied STOP to this sender. Use another number, or reply START from it. Nothing was saved.
sms.testFailed_unreachable: No response arrived from the SMS provider. The test text may have been sent. Check the test phone or the provider's message log before retrying. Check the server's internet access, DNS, and provider base URL. Nothing was saved.
sms.invalidPhone: Enter a valid phone number. Start it with + and its country code (for example +1 604 555 0123), or set the gym's country code in Settings → Gym details.
sms.twilioOnly: This install accepts only Twilio’s provider URL.
email.title: Email
email.unreadable: Your stored SMTP settings could not be read. Replace or remove them. Email uses the fallback shown below.
email.sourceGym: Sends through your own SMTP service: {host}, port {port} ({security}), from {from}.
email.sourceInstall: Uses this install’s email settings (the SMTP_* values on the server).
email.sourceNone: No email service is set up: the gym can’t send email.
email.hint: Use an SMTP sending service such as Postmark, Brevo, or Amazon SES. The settings are saved only after a test email is accepted.
email.hostHint: Your sending service's SMTP server, not your gym's own domain. For example, Mailgun uses smtp.mailgun.org and SendGrid uses smtp.sendgrid.net.
email.secure: Use TLS from the start (usually port 465)
email.portMismatch_tls: Implicit TLS is on, but the port isn't 465. Most services use implicit TLS only on port 465: clear this box for port 587 or 2525.
email.portMismatch_starttls: Port 465 usually needs implicit TLS. Tick this box, or use port 587 or 2525.
email.fromHint: The From address, on a domain your sending service has verified. It is usually not your SMTP username (Mailgun's username looks like postmaster@mg.example.org).
email.confirmSignIn: I understand how people will sign in after this change
email.saved: Test email sent. The new email settings are saved.
email.testFailed: The test email failed. Check the settings and try again; nothing was saved.
email.testFailed_connection: The test email failed: the app couldn't connect to the SMTP server. Check the hostname and port; some hosting providers block ports 25, 465 and 587, so try 2525. Nothing was saved.
email.testFailed_tls: The test email failed: the secure connection didn't start, or the server didn't offer a secure connection on this port. Implicit TLS should be on for port 465 and off for ports 587 and 2525; if that is already right, use the port your service lists for secure sending. Nothing was saved.
email.testFailed_authentication: The test email failed: the SMTP server refused the username or password, or it won't send mail without a login. Check the username, the password and the SMTP hostname. Nothing was saved.
email.testFailed_sender_refused: The test email failed: the SMTP server refused the message. Check that the sender address is on a domain your service has verified and that the test recipient is valid. Nothing was saved.
email.lastFailed_connection: The last email, at {at}, failed: the app couldn't connect to the sending service.
email.lastFailed_tls: The last email, at {at}, failed: the secure connection didn't start.
email.lastFailed_authentication: The last email, at {at}, failed: the service rejected the login. Test and save the current password below.
email.lastFailed_sender_refused: The last email, at {at}, failed: the service refused the sender address.
email.remove: Remove and use the install’s settings
email.removeNone: Remove (the gym will have no email)
email.removed: The gym’s own email settings are removed.
email.onlySignIn: Email links are your only way to sign in, since your account has no password. Removing email would lock you out.
email.googleRemovalRule: The removal check counts Google when it is configured for this gym. It does not check whether your account can use it. Before removing email, sign out and confirm you can sign in with Google, or set a password while password sign-in is enabled.
email.notConfigured: The gym has no email settings of its own.
payments.title: Payments
payments.notConfigured: Stripe isn’t connected: members can’t pay by card.
payments.webhookRegistered: Webhook endpoint registered: Stripe sends payment updates to this gym.
payments.locked: Members have Stripe customers, cards or payments, so a new key must be for the same Stripe account and mode.
payments.hint: Use a restricted key from your Stripe Dashboard with the permissions listed in setup. The key is checked, and the webhook endpoint is kept or replaced, before anything is saved.
payments.invalid: Enter a restricted key beginning with rk_test_ or rk_live_.
payments.saved: The new Stripe key is saved.
payments.missingPermission: Stripe refused one of the key’s permissions. Check them against the list in setup and try again.
payments.accountLocked: This key is for another Stripe account, so it wasn’t saved. The gym’s Stripe customers, saved cards and card payments were made in the current account, and another account can’t charge or refund them. Use a key from the current account.
payments.modeLocked: Customers, cards and payments exist in the current mode, so the key can’t switch between test and live.
payments.modeLockedLive: Live Stripe customers, cards or payments exist, so a test key can’t replace the live one.
payments.inProgress: A payment or refund is still being processed. A refund reservation that never reached Stripe clears automatically after 23 hours, within the next hourly check. If still blocked after 24 hours, ask an owner or admin to check Stripe and payment reconciliation.
payments.lockedTest: Members have test-mode Stripe customers, cards or payments. A new test key must be for the same Stripe account. A live key can replace it once you confirm clearing the test data.
payments.importedOnly: Households have Stripe customer IDs from an import, and nothing else ties the gym to a Stripe account yet, so a key from any account is accepted. With a live key, customers the account can’t read get new ones the first time they pay or save a card. A test key can’t read live customers, so with one, those households’ payment and card links aren’t available.
payments.switchIntro: The gym has Stripe customers, cards or payments in test mode. Switching to the live key clears the test-mode Stripe data after the key is checked, so members start fresh in live mode.
payments.switchCustomers: Households’ test Stripe customers: {count}. Each gets a live customer the first time they pay or save a card.
payments.switchCards: Saved test cards: {count}. Members save a card again.
payments.switchCheckouts: Open Stripe payment and card pages: {count}. Their links still work and open a live page.
payments.switchDisputes: Open test disputes: {count}. They close, since the live account can’t read or answer them.
payments.switchPayments: Test card payments: {count}. They stay on their invoices, marked “Stripe test mode”.
payments.switchImported: Imported Stripe customers: {customers}, and imported cards: {cards}. An import may hold the gym’s live ones. A customer the live account can’t read gets a new one the first time that member pays or saves a card.
payments.switchBooks: Invoices, memberships, cash payments and everything else in the gym.
payments.switchFinal: Once live customers, cards or payments exist, the gym can’t go back to test mode.
payments.switchConfirm: I understand the test data listed above is cleared
payments.switch: Clear test data and switch to live
payments.switched: Stripe is now in live mode. The test customers, cards and payment pages were cleared; test payments stay, marked “Stripe test mode”.
payments.failed: Stripe couldn’t check the key. Check the key and your connection, then try again.
backups.title: Backups
backups.notConfigured: Backups aren’t set up. Updates refuse to run until they are.
backups.noneUnderKey: No restorable snapshot under this key at the current destination yet.
backups.snapshotUnknown: The last snapshot couldn’t be checked.
backups.retention: Retention budget: {size}. Snapshots keep 24 hourly, 7 nightly, 4 weekly, and up to 2 pre-upgrade copies when space allows.
backups.changeWarning: After a change, new snapshots use the new destination and key, starting right after you confirm. Snapshots under the old key stay readable only with that key until retention removes them, so keep the old key until then. A new bucket starts empty, and the app no longer manages the old one: its snapshots stay there until you delete them.
backups.hint: Snapshots are encrypted before uploading. Only your backup private key can open them.
backups.secretAccessKey: S3 secret access key (not the Cloudflare API token value)
backups.pending: A new destination (bucket {bucket}) and key wait for you to confirm the private key. Until then, snapshots keep using the current settings.
backups.savedKey: I saved my private key somewhere safe
backups.confirmed: Backups now use the new destination and key.
backups.noPending: Generate a new backup key first.
backups.unreachable: The storage destination refused the request. Check the endpoint, region, bucket and access keys; nothing was changed.
backups.credentialsHint: Use this after rotating the storage access key. The endpoint, bucket, backup key and existing snapshots stay the same.
backups.credentialsReplaced: Backups now use the new storage credentials. The destination, backup key and snapshots are unchanged.
backups.credentialsUnreachable: The storage destination refused the new credentials. Check the access key ID and secret; nothing was changed.
